analysis.one_liner: Hindalco is India's largest aluminium and copper producer (Aditya Birla Group), and parent of Novelis, the world's largest aluminium rolled-products and recycling company supplying the auto, beverage-can and aerospace industries globally.
analysis.whats_happening: Hindalco reported Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended September 2026, announced around November 6, 2026): consolidated revenue of Rs 91,708 crore, up 39% year-on-year, and PAT of Rs 7,533 crore, up 59% year-on-year, helped by a record Copper segment and a stronger India aluminium upstream business, even as EBITDA actually eased quarter-on-quarter and LME aluminium prices softened to about $3,227/tonne from $3,576/tonne. The next results date (for the December 2026 quarter) has not been announced yet; based on last year's pattern it would fall around January-February 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of Hindalco as two businesses stitched together: an Indian aluminium-and-copper mining and smelting operation, and Novelis, a US-headquartered subsidiary that turns raw aluminium into sheet metal for cars and drink cans worldwide - Novelis alone is more than half of group revenue. The uncomfortable part: Novelis's big new US plant at Bay Minette, Alabama has seen its cost estimate roughly double, from about $2.5 billion to around $5 billion, and commercial shipments have slipped to the quarter ending June 2027. Meanwhile the group's net debt relative to EBITDA has climbed from 1.23x to 1.80x in a year. So current profits look strong, but the growth bet behind them is costing more and taking longer than planned.
analysis.quarters: Revenue and PAT have grown steadily over the last five quarters, culminating in Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 91,708 crore (+39% YoY) and PAT of Rs 7,533 crore (+59% YoY). But the series is not fully comparable: Q4 FY26 (quarter ended March 2026) carried an exceptional loss of roughly Rs 4,565 crore tied to two fires at Novelis's Oswego, New York plant (September and November 2025); stripping that out, underlying Q4 FY26 PAT was closer to Rs 5,796 crore, up 10% YoY, not the reported 51% YoY fall. Separately, management flagged that Q2 FY27's record Copper EBITDA of Rs 1,673 crore (+164% YoY) was partly boosted by one-time by-product gains, so that jump overstates the segment's run-rate profitability. On the earnings call, management said the Novelis Oswego hot mill was back to normal output and described the roughly Rs 50,000 crore multi-year capex plan as 'on track.'
analysis.performance_read: The stock closed at Rs 960, down 16.1% from a May 2026 peak of Rs 1,143.73, but still comfortably inside its 52-week range of Rs 770.63-1,143.73 - this looks like a normal pullback, not a crash, and there is no recent demerger or spin-off in the supplied data to adjust for (the only corporate action on record is a 10:1 split from 2005, long before any of the return windows below). Over 1 year the stock is up 22.9% versus a 2.13% fall in the Nifty and a 47.71% fall in peer Vedanta; over 3 years it is up 103.13% versus 28.85% for the Nifty and 33.94% for Vedanta; over 5 years it is up 113.75% versus 38.72% for the Nifty and 64.56% for Vedanta. Hindalco has clearly outpaced both the index and its closest listed peer over every horizon shown.
analysis.valuation_read: At Rs 960, Hindalco trades around 9.3x trailing earnings and about 1.35x book value, against an ROE of 13.0% and ROCE of 13.2% - on the surface, that looks inexpensive for a business earning double-digit returns on capital. Why it is cheap: it is a cyclical commodity producer whose earnings move with global aluminium and copper prices, and it is in the middle of a large, now more expensive and delayed capex cycle (Bay Minette) funded partly by rising debt. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether current profits - flattered partly by one-off gains this quarter - and a softening LME aluminium price hold up; if either falters while debt keeps climbing, the multiple could look less cheap in hindsight.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has been both volume- and margin-led, but unevenly across segments: India Aluminium Upstream EBITDA rose 55% YoY to Rs 7,009 crore and Novelis revenue grew 25% YoY in dollar terms, both reflecting genuine volume and pricing gains. The Copper segment's 164% YoY EBITDA jump to a record Rs 1,673 crore is the outlier - management itself attributed part of it to one-time by-product gains, so that segment's growth is less durable than the headline number implies.
analysis.health_read: Operating cash generation has broadly tracked profit growth, but the balance sheet has gotten more leveraged: net debt stood at about Rs 80,435 crore as of September 2026, and net debt/EBITDA rose from 1.23x a year earlier to 1.80x now, driven by the India and Novelis capex programmes. The core aluminium and copper businesses themselves look healthy (double-digit ROCE, rising segment profits); the bigger risk here is financial - how much more debt the Bay Minette cost overrun requires, and whether cash flow keeps pace - rather than an operating problem.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Aditya Birla Group, via IGH Holdings Pvt Ltd at roughly 15.77% and Grasim Industries at roughly 3.92%, among others) held 34.67% as of September 2026, with no pledging reported. Foreign institutional investors held 30.17% and domestic institutions 20.97%, including LIC at roughly 4.33% (this LIC figure comes from a secondary source and could not be independently confirmed on Screener). There is no widely-tracked individual celebrity investor on the register based on available data - the shareholder base is institutional rather than built around a single marquee name.
strengths: PAT grew 59% YoY to Rs 7,533 crore in Q2 FY27 on broad-based segment growth
India Aluminium Upstream EBITDA up 55% YoY to Rs 7,009 crore, a genuine volume-and-price gain
Promoter holding steady at 34.67% with zero pledging as of September 2026
Valuation of ~9.3x earnings and ~1.35x book sits below an ROE of 13.0% and ROCE of 13.2%
watchpoints: Net debt/EBITDA has risen from 1.23x to 1.80x in a year as capex ramps up
Novelis's Bay Minette plant cost has roughly doubled from about $2.5 billion to around $5 billion, with commercial shipments now pushed to the quarter ending June 2027
Two fires at Novelis's Oswego, NY plant drove a roughly Rs 4,565 crore exceptional charge in Q4 FY26, making that quarter's reported PAT non-comparable to others
EBITDA fell quarter-on-quarter in Q2 FY27 even as PAT rose, alongside softening LME aluminium prices (~$3,227/tonne versus ~$3,576/tonne the prior quarter)
analysis.one_thing: Whether Novelis's Bay Minette plant - now costing roughly $5 billion versus an original $2.5 billion, with commercial shipments delayed to the quarter ending June 2027 - ramps up on the revised budget and timeline will determine whether the group's rising leverage (net debt/EBITDA now 1.80x) pays off or becomes a lasting drag.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly P&L, valuation ratios, and shareholding figures cross-checked primarily via Screener.in and company/exchange filings, supplemented by earnings-call commentary and news reports. Not independently verified: EV/EBITDA (sources showed a wide range, roughly 7x to 12x, likely a TTM-versus-trailing-FY mismatch), the exact date of the next (Q3 FY27) results, and the LIC shareholding figure, which came from a secondary source. EBITDA figures for some quarters varied by up to roughly Rs 900 crore across sources depending on how other income was treated; the more conservative operating-profit figure was used throughout.
